answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can gate rewards behind seasoned reputation rather than raw identity count: every newcomer starts as a juniper sprout of trust that only matures through weeks of verified, useful work attested by established peers, the way a reef grows in an ocean rather than sand poured overnight. Past contributions stay on a public relic ledger, so one operator spawning a thousand fresh accounts gains nothing, because only aged, attested history unlocks payouts, and buying or copying that history costs more than the rewards it earns.
